value.name: Ava Community Energy
value.notes: Ava Community Energy (formerly East Bay Community Energy) confirms Albany as a current member city, alongside Berkeley, Dublin, Emeryville, Fremont, Hayward, Livermore, Newark, Oakland, Piedmont, Pleasanton, San Leandro, and Union City in Alameda County. value.name: California SGIP - current category and budget check required
value.description: New applications and waitlist applications for ratepayer-funded SGIP budgets closed on December 30, 2025. New AB 209 applications have a June 30, 2028 deadline. The 2026 SGIP rate table publishes $3.10/W for solar and $1.10/Wh for storage in applicable Residential Solar and Storage Equity categories. Household eligibility and live budget availability vary by category and program administrator; check the official Program Metrics tracker before relying on an incentive.
value.eligibility: Eligibility varies by 2026 SGIP budget category, program administrator, property, income/pathway, project rules, and live funding availability.

battery_programs.notes: SGIP program data refreshed on 2026-08-26 from the official 2026 Handbook and live Program Metrics. Earlier locality records contained 2025 opening/availability language. This record does not assert household eligibility, reservation availability, or a guaranteed incentive; current category and program-administrator status must be checked before reliance.

value: Schedule inspections by calling (510) 528-5760 or emailing permits@albanyca.org; next-day inspections are typically possible, but allow up to 3 days lead time
To cancel a scheduled inspection, call no later than 9:00am on the day of the inspection
A five-working-day advance notice may be required for a Final Inspection
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Division inspection scheduling process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.program_or_pathway: Small Residential Rooftop Solar Systems streamlined permitting process (§12-14)
other_conditions: Streamlined process covers systems no larger than 10kW AC nameplate rating or 30kW thermal
Systems must meet applicable health and safety standards required by the State and the City of Albany Fire Department
Water-heating systems must be certified by an accredited listing agency per the California Building Standards Code
Electricity-producing systems must meet standards from the California Building Standards Code, IEEE, and accredited testing laboratories (e.g. UL)
Routine operation and maintenance does not require a permit
